title: Polynomial-Time Computability of Work Fragments
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state binary Turing machine, let a binary code be given for its optional states, and let $	au$ be one of its work tapes. If $t$ assigns a natural number to each bit string and the unary string of length $t(z)$ is polynomial-time computable as a function of $z$, then the work fragment for tape $	au$ at time $t(z)$ is polynomial-time computable as a function of $z$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite-state binary Turing machine
A binary code is given for the optional states of $M$
$	au$ is a work tape of $M$
$t$ is a function from bit strings to natural numbers
The unary string of length $t(z)$ is polynomial-time computable as a function of $z$
replaced: For every source machine, state code, work tape, and polynomial-time unary time producer, the serialized work fragment at the produced time is polynomial-time computable, with the greatest-earlier source address read from the protected visit table.
